blocks.text: Family of man killed by tiger criticise online content as Trump mocks fatal incident
The family of a British man who was killed by a tiger at a wildlife park have spoken of their “severe distress” after Donald Trump shared a video of the incident on social media.
The president posted footage of William Chapman, 23, being fatally attacked by a tiger at the Yorkshire Wildlife Park to 13m followers on his Truth Social platform on Tuesday evening.
Trump accompanied the short clip – which showed the animal biting and clawing Chapman as he sat in the enclosure, but not him being killed – with the signed message: “Don’t ever mess with nature!”
On Wednesday morning Trump followed this up with another post – this time an AI-generated video of him grappling with a tiger, which appears to mimic the original.
The clip, which is accompanied by the song ‘The Lion Sleeps Tonight’, features the president copying the pointing gesture made by Chapman and ends with him hugging the animal.
Chapman’s family said in a statement that “deeply offensive media content is causing them severe distress”.

They also posted a tribute describing him as a “bright, warm and engaging young man” and questioning what part his “significant mental illness over a number of years” and prescribed strong medication played in the incident.
Trump heads to Arizona and Montana after campaign stop-off in conservative Alaska
Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog.
Donald Trump will attend campaign rallies in Arizona and Montana later today, having spent the past 24 hours in Alaska – a sign of his party’s recent polling woes.
Conservative Alaska is one of several where the Democrats have a chance of flipping a Senate seat amid voter dissatisfaction with the cost of living and the Iran war.
Polling has shown Democratic candidate Mary Peltola tied ⁠or slightly ahead of incumbent Republican senator Dan ⁠Sullivan in a state the president carried by 14 percentage points in 2024.

Here, as in much of the United States, the president’s approval rating is flopping, hit by rising diesel and gasoline prices and a conflict in the Middle East that has proven deeply unpopular with voters.

Opening for Trump, Sullivan acknowledged that Alaskans face “challenges” when it comes to energy costs. But “the conflict in the Middle East is temporary,” he said. “The true forever war is the national Democrats’ war against Alaska oil and gas ⁠and our jobs.“
The president has taken to campaigning in conservative-leaning ​parts of competitive states, rather than in more politically diverse areas with more votes potentially up for grabs.
At one point, Trump pardoned two local repair shop owners who were convicted of violating the federal Clean Air Act for removing pollution controls on diesel engines.
He also encouraged Republicans to vote by mail – a process he has repeatedly sought to curtail and discredit. Trump will spend Wednesday campaigning in Arizona and Montana.
In other developments:

items: In Alaska, Donald Trump repeated his false claim that he had to start his war on Iran because, “they were two weeks away from having a nuclear weapon”. In fact, US intelligence agencies reported to Congress in 2025 that Iran had suspended its pursuit of nuclear weapons in 2003. Despite that assessment, in the summer of 2025, Trump ordered the US bombing of Iran’s nuclear enrichment facilities which he later claimed had “obliterated” the country’s nuclear program. Eight months after that, he launched a full-scale war on Iran justified, he now says, by Iran being just weeks away from getting the bomb.

blocks.text: Good morning. Pope Leo XIV, the head of the 1.4 billion-strong Roman Catholic church, has been diagnosed with lung cancer. articles.title: Nvidia, worth $5.5tn, donates $250m to UK for AI safety research
articles.summary:
Pledge spanning five years from world’s most valuable firm comes as concerns about AI agents have risen

The $5.5tn (£4.1tn) US chipmaker Nvidia is donating $250m worth of computing power to…

blocks.text: The $5.5tn (£4.1tn) US chipmaker Nvidia is donating $250m worth of computing power to the UK to support AI safety research.

The donation from the world’s most valuable company comes as the UK government confirmed its AI Security Institute, which tests advance AI models, will be able to examine cutting-edge technology developed by companies such as OpenAI, Anthropic and Google before they are released.
Nvidia said the donation, which spans five years, would “support agentic safety and security research across the UK”.

Safety concerns about AI agents – highly capable computer programs that are able to design and perform sequences of tasks autonomously – have risen since the summer, when OpenAI confirmed that a “swarm” of agents had attacked Hugging Face, a tech startup.

Nvidia did not reference AISI in its statement but said most of the money would “support the wider UK AI safety and security research community”, with a proportion of the cash going to the -led British Open-Ended Learning and Discovery Lab, the Science of Fundamental AI Research Lab – run by the Edinburgh, Cambridge, Oxford and University College London universities – and Imperial College London.

“The UK brings world-class scientific rigour to this essential engineering challenge,” said Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s chief executive. “With this $250m commitment, Nvidia will put accelerated computing in the hands of UK researchers to develop, test and strengthen safeguards for increasingly powerful AI.”

articles.title: JV Ejercito flags ‘major changes’ in House-approved 2027 budget bill
articles.summary: 'The cuts to preventive health programs are substantial, while medical assistance has increased,' says Senate finance committee chairperson JV Ejercito

blocks.text: PRIVILEGE SPEECH. Senate Deputy Majority Leader JV Ejercito delivers a privilege speech during the Senate plenary session on January 27.
Senate Social Media Unit
'The cuts to preventive health programs are substantial, while medical assistance has increased,' says Senate finance committee chairperson JV Ejercito

items: Senate finance committee chairperson JV Ejercito criticized the House-approved version of the 2027 budget over significant cuts to preventive health programs and infrastructure projects, including reductions in immunization and health facility enhancement funding.

The House version of the budget increased funding for medical assistance programs while making substantial cuts to preventive health care, raising concerns about the implications for Universal Health Care.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – Senate finance committee chairperson JV Ejercito on Wednesday, October 14, flagged billions of pesos in reductions to preventive health programs and infrastructure projects in the House-approved version of the P7.2-trillion 2027 general appropriations bill (GAB).

Ejercito said in a news briefing that the House version of the budget bill, which the Senate formally received on Tuesday, had major changes compared to the 2027 National Expenditure Program (NEP), including a P130-billion reduction in foreign-assisted projects, a P9.5-billion cut in calamity funds, and billions of pesos in reductions to health programs.

The “major changes” include a P4-billion reduction in the Department of Health’s (DOH) immunization program and a P4.5-billion cut in the DOH-Health Facilities Enhancement Program (HFEP), which funds the improvement and expansion of government health facilities. He also cited a P2.6-billion reduction in right-of-way funding and a P4.6-billion cut in funding for flood mitigation structures within major river basins.

The House version of the budget bill increased funding for the DOH’s Medical Assistance to Indigent and Financially Incapacitated Patients (MAIFIP) by P23.9 billion, allocated P10 billion for a new Presidential Assistance to Farmers and Fisherfolk program under the Department of Agriculture, and added P8.04 billion for flood mitigation structures under the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH).

“The cuts to preventive health programs are substantial, while medical assistance has increased. This is a puzzle for me because one of the key factors of Universal Health Care (UHC) is strengthening preventive care, yet that is what they reduced,” Ejercito said in Filipino.
“What are we supposed to do with this? Remove funding for immunization and health promotion, then provide medical assistance when people get sick?” he added.

Ejercito said the Senate received the House-approved GAB late Tuesday afternoon, and that copies have been distributed to the senators. An October 23 deadline was set for the Senate finance committee vice chairpersons to submit their committee reports.
The Senate temporarily paused from its impeachment court duties starting October 14 in view of the ongoing committee hearings for the proposed 2027 national budget.

Ejercito said the chamber is targeting to finish all budget-related committee hearings by October 23 before it goes on a brief recess. The senator also said he is eyeing to sponsor the 2027 budget bill in the Senate plenary by November 23, and have it approved by the second week of December.

“We are also planning to continue what Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian did when he was the finance chairperson — livestream the bicameral conference committee to ensure transparency. We are also keeping in touch with CSOs, the academe, and other watchdogs and will meet them to hear their observations on October 26,” said Ejercito.

The House of Representatives approved the proposed 2027 budget on Monday amid concerns from some lawmakers and civil society organizations (CSOs) that the spending plan is riddled with pork barrel allocations. – Rappler.com

articles.title: CICC warns of online grooming tactics, from love-bombing to blackmail
articles.summary: The Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC) on Wednesday warned that online grooming involves several stages of manipulation, including isolation, love-bombing and blackmail, which…

blocks.text: Published October 14, 2026 6:03pm

The Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC) on Wednesday warned that online grooming involves several stages of manipulation, including isolation, love-bombing and blackmail, which could lead to violence or suicide among young victims.

Speaking at the Bagong Pilipinas Ngayon public briefing, CICC Executive Director Undersecretary Renato Paraiso said nihilistic violent extremism (NVE), which authorities suspect may have contributed to a series of school shootings, involves different levels of manipulation that could lead to various outcomes.

Paraiso said online groomers typically target children through gaming and social media platforms, where they assess their potential victims' interests, including their attitudes toward violence and sexual content, before befriending them.
“After that, they move [victims] to messaging platforms such as Discord and Telegram, which are more private. There are also communities within these platforms,” Paraiso said.
He said groomers then attempt to gain their victims' trust and emotional dependence through a tactic known as love-bombing.
“In those communities, they make [victims] feel loved through what we call love-bombing. The goal is for the group to replace the family structure,” he added.
NVE refers to an extremist mindset that embraces violence, destruction or mass harm without necessarily pursuing a conventional political, religious or ideological goal.

Unlike traditional extremist movements, which often seek to advance a defined cause or worldview, NVE may be driven by nihilism, alienation, a desire for notoriety or an online community's glorification of violence.
According to Paraiso, groomers initially ask victims to perform seemingly harmless tasks, such as taking selfies, while offering praise and encouragement to gain their trust.
The demands gradually escalate to more serious and potentially incriminating acts, including committing crimes or sending nude photographs.
Paraiso said groomers could then use these materials to blackmail victims, threatening to release the images or expose their actions if they tell their families about the abuse.
He warned that the final stage of manipulation could lead to extreme violence or suicide, although not all cases result in school shootings.
“In the final stage, victims may either carry out school shootings or, more commonly, although we do not always see it, young people take their own lives,” Paraiso said.
The warning comes amid concerns over three school shooting incidents reported in the Philippines in 2026.
In June, three students were killed when two suspects opened fire on their classmates at a public high school in Tacloban City.
In August, a student shot a schoolmate before turning the gun on himself in Zamboanga.
A similar incident occurred in South Cotabato in September, when a student shot a schoolmate before taking his own life.— MCG, GMA News

In about a month, Rappler will be holding Social Good Summit 2026, which will be all about upskilling people to survive and thrive amid artificial intelligence — the risks it poses, and the opportunities it presents.

articles.title: Trump announces plans for major oil, gas and mineral exploration in Greenland
articles.summary: The US president has claimed Greenland holds vast and easily accessible oil reserves without providing evidence or details. His announcement follows a deal expanding the US military presence on the…

image.caption: Greenland's vast natural resources have attracted growing US interest, with President Donald Trump announcing plans for major oil, gas and mineral exploration (FILE 19/07/2008)Image: Ashley Cooper/Pond5 Images/IMAGO

blocks.text: US President Donald Trump on Wednesday said major oil, gas and mineral exploration was set to begin in Greenland.
His announcement follows a security agreement between the United States, Denmark and the Arctic island's leaders.
What has Trump said about Greenland's resources?
Trump offered no details about which companies would be involved, where exploration would take place or when operations would begin.
"Massive Oil, Gas, and Mineral Exploration is getting ready to begin in our new and beautiful Greenland!" Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform.
He also claimed that experts believed Greenland held some of the world's largest deposits of easily accessible oil, without providing evidence.

Greenland is believed to hold substantial untapped oil reserves, but their commercial viability remains uncertain due to high extraction costs, harsh Arctic conditions and environmental restrictions. No commercial oil production has been established in Greenland.
Greenland has significant mineral resources, including rare earth elements used in electronics, renewable energy technologies and military equipment.
What's really in the Greenland deal?
The island has also attracted interest for its potential oil and gas reserves, although exploration in the harsh Arctic environment presents considerable technical and economic challenges.
In August, reports that a US oil company was preparing operations in a remote part of eastern Greenland prompted unease among residents and local authorities.
Trump did not say whether his announcement was connected to those activities.
Why is Greenland strategically important to the US?
In the same post, Trump described Greenland's strategic location as "second to none" for US and European security.
"Any future attack on the United States will have to come across Greenland," he claimed, adding that US defenses there would be able to intercept missiles, drones and other weapons.
Greenland lies along one of the shortest routes between Russia and North America, making it strategically important for missile detection and defense.
Its location is also significant for Trump's proposed "Golden Dome" missile defense system.
Melting Arctic ice has meanwhile increased interest in potential new shipping routes through the region.
What does the US security deal with Greenland involve?
In September, the United States, Denmark and Greenland signed an agreement aimed at easing tensions after Trump's repeated threats to take control of the island, including by force.
Under the 10-page agreement, Washington will establish two additional military bases, at Narsarsuaq in southern Greenland and Mestersvig in the east.
The US already operates the Pituffik Space Base in northern Greenland.

The agreement expands the American military presence and provides for cooperation on missile defense, while reaffirming Danish sovereignty over Greenland and the Greenlandic people's right to self-determination.
Greenland is a self-governing territory within the Kingdom of Denmark.
Trump's earlier demands for US control of the island had strained relations between Washington and Copenhagen, both NATO allies.

articles.title: ‘Like being in a vortex’: US report details extent of ‘devastating’ dating-app scams
articles.summary:
Congress calls for Match Group and others to do more to help victims like Mary, who lost $100,000 to app scammer

Mary met a man on the dating app Plenty of Fish in 2024. She told the…

blocks.text: Mary met a man on the dating app Plenty of Fish in 2024. She told the Guardian she had been looking for a connection, but instead became the victim of a romance scam that cost her almost $100,000.

“There was a lot of conversation, and then it started with the constant contact, pressure and repeated asks for money,” Mary, who asked that her last name be withheld, said in an interview on Tuesday. “It just escalated really, really quickly.”

Mary was one of several people who spoke to staffers from the US Congress’s joint economic committee as part of an investigation by senators Maggie Hassan, Democrat of New Hampshire, and Marsha Blackburn, Republican of Tennessee, into romance scams on dating platforms owned by Match Group. Match Group operates apps such as Tinder, Hinge, Plenty of Fish, Match (formerly Match.com) and others.

“Romance scams, in which fraudsters form relationships to induce money or gifts from victims, have become a leading form of financial fraud in the United States and cost Americans at least $1.3bn annually,” the senators noted upon the investigation’s launch last September.
On Tuesday, a report detailing the results of that investigation was published.

Internal documents provided by Match Group showed that “as of the second half of 2025, Tinder had not updated most of its machine learning models in years” and “as a result, Tinder detected scammers and other bad actors less reliably and struggled to keep pace with emerging threats”, per the report.

Data provided by Match Group also showed that through the third quarter of 2025 in the US, nearly 1.5m scammers or other bad actors on Tinder and Hinge had “matched with at least one other user”. The report also showed that nearly 500,000 of those accounts “exchanged contact information with another user”.

Mary told the Guardian that she tried to establish whether the scammer she spoke with was real. He would contact her constantly, she said, and knew where she lived. She said that the man told her he needed money for work-related things and medical emergencies.

“They never leave you alone,” she said. “I call it like being in a vortex. You don’t even realise what’s happening. You’re sending money, and it’s adding up, but each one of those times that you send money, it’s, like, not connected to the other times. But finally when I realized how much money I lost, I was like: ‘Whoa.’”
In total, Mary said she sent the man about $100,000 in cryptocurrency payments. After realizing he was a scammer, she blocked his number. He would then switch phone numbers and contact her again.
Mary has since sought to identify the people behind the fraud and discovered other Plenty of Fish profiles using the same photos as the man she had talked to. She has reported them to the platform.
“If you knew me, you would say she would never do that,” Mary said, adding that she struggles to understand how it all happened, but believes it’s “really a lot about force of control”.

Tuesday’s report noted that since the launch of the investigation last September, Match Group has “introduced and expanded important measures designed to combat scams” including a facial verification feature on the Tinder app across the US, “requiring all new Tinder users to complete a video selfie verification process”.

In a news release on Tuesday, Hassan and committee Democrats added that Match Group also “instituted new efforts designed to remove harmful accounts more effectively” including in the first half of 2025, a “new AI model” that examines profiles and other information to detect scammers and other bad actors.

“It is encouraging that following committee outreach, Match Group introduced new AI models,” the report states. However, those “changes came after a prolonged period during which scams continued to proliferate on Tinder”.
after newsletter promotion

In response to the report on Tuesday, Yoel Roth, Match Group’s senior vice-president of trust and safety said in a statement: “We’re grateful the committee recognized our significant advancements to protect our users against romance scams.”

He said: “That said, the report mischaracterizes both the historical scale of our investment and the work already complete. Alongside our engagement with the Committee over the past year, we’ve made the largest safety advancements in Match Group’s history. Trust and safety is a foundational priority, and we intend to continue leading the industry in building tools that promote authentic, safe connections.”
Much of the safety work, including face check, was already under way before the committee’s investigation, Match Group told NBC News.

In June, Hassan introduced legislation alongside with Republican senator Rick Scott, that would establish a central portal for Americans to report scams “and get the help they need from law enforcement and agencies”.

Hassan, in a statement along with the release of the report on Tuesday, described romance scams as “devastating – both financially and emotionally – to people who are looking for connection and instead find themselves targeted and exploited by global criminal enterprises”.
“During the course of our investigation, Match Group made progress in combating scammers – but it shouldn’t have taken so long, and there’s still more that Match needs to do,” she said.

“As criminal networks use AI to supercharge their scams, dating apps and all companies must quickly and proactively keep their scam defenses up to date. Companies must stay vigilant and prioritize comprehensive scam prevention at every level to protect consumers and block fraudsters from infiltrating online platforms.”

articles.title: 51% of Pinoys want Sara Duterte to testify in impeachment trial — poll
articles.summary: At least 51% of Filipino adults want Vice President Sara Duterte to appear before the Senate impeachment court to personally testify in the trial, according to the latest report by public opinion…

blocks.text: October 14, 2026 | 5:54pm
Vice President Sara Duterte arrives before the start of the impeachment trial at the Senate of the Philippines in Pasay, Metro Manila on July 7, 2026.
Noel Celis, pool / AFP

MANILA, Philippines — At least 51% of Filipino adults want Vice President Sara Duterte to appear before the Senate impeachment court to personally testify in the trial, according to the latest report by public opinion polling firm Pulse Asia Research Inc.

Pulse Asia’s nationwide survey results, which were released on Wednesday, October 14, indicate that a narrow majority of respondents said they want to hear Duterte’s personal testimony in the impeachment trial against her.
Only 34% said Duterte should not personally appear and testify before the Senate impeachment court, while 14% were undecided and 1% refused to answer.
The survey was conducted from September 17 to 24 through face-to-face interviews with 2,400 Filipino adults aged 18 and older. It has a ±2% margin of error at the 95% confidence level.
Opinions vary across regions

Opinions on Duterte’s personal testimony differ by region, with the majority of respondents in Luzon reflecting the national survey results, while the majority of respondents from Visayas and Mindanao expressed otherwise.

In the National Capital Region (NCR), 66% said they want the vice president’s personal testimony, while 21% said the opposite. At least 61% of respondents in Balance Luzon, meanwhile, said they believe Duterte should personally testify, while 20% said she should not.

In Visayas, only 43% of respondents said Duterte should personally appear before the Senate impeachment court, while an equal share expressed the opposite view, 11% remained undecided, and 2% refused to answer.

Meanwhile, the contrasting view is more prevalent in Duterte’s stronghold of Mindanao, as only 32% said they preferred the vice president’s personal testimony, while 61% said she should not. Only 7% said they “can’t say,” while no one refused to answer.
Unexplained wealth
The survey also found that the number of people who believed that the unexplained wealth allegations against the vice president were likely to be true had increased in September.
Compared with July's 27% record, 29% of respondents in September said they believed the unexplained wealth allegations could be true, reflecting a 2-percentage-point increase.
The number of people who believed that the accusations were likely to be untrue, meanwhile, decreased by 8 percentage points, from 38% in July to 30% in September.
The number of those who could not say whether the allegations were true or untrue, meanwhile, also climbed from 32% in July to 39% in September, showing a 7-percentage-point increase.
In July, Duterte appeared on the premises of the Senate but did not attend the trial and met with her counselors instead.
The Senate impeachment rules allow the vice president to appear either personally or through counsel before the Senate impeachment court.
Recently, the prosecutors dropped three impeachment charges against Duterte, keeping only the alleged unexplained wealth charge.

articles.title: Charlottetown police lost the evidence in a P.E.I. cold-case murder. How did it happen?

image.caption: Byron Carr, a teacher at Montague Regional High School, was found strangled and stabbed in in his home on Lapthorne Avenue nearly 38 years ago. (Submitted)

blocks.text: PEI·New

The case against the man accused of murdering a P.E.I. teacher in 1988 has unravelled after Charlottetown police revealed the evidence crucial to securing a conviction was missing. How did police lose key evidence, and what does that mean for the case?
‘Nothing he could be sentenced to would ever bring Byron back,’ says victim’s brother

All charges against Todd Joseph Irving, 59, were dropped on Tuesday. He had been charged with first-degree murder and interfering with human remains in the killing of Byron Carr, a teacher found strangled and stabbed in his home.

According to the P.E.I. Crown Attorney's Office, moving forward with prosecution wasn’t an option because Charlottetown Police Services lost key evidence, leaving no chance of a conviction at the trial that was scheduled to begin in November.

items: Charges laid in decades-old P.E.I. cold case murder withdrawn after key evidence lost
Family of Byron Carr speaks out after murder charges in decades-old cold case withdrawn

blocks.text: Darren MacDougall, Charlottetown's interim police chief, told CBC News on Tuesday that the agency knew when the cold case was reopened in 2007 — long before Irving was charged in early 2024 — that the knife left at the scene and the towel used to strangle Carr were missing.
“This was 1988. It was a different time in policing, the standards were far different than they are today,” MacDougall said.
So police instead built their case on DNA found at the scene.

“What we did in 2007 was we endeavoured to look at what we had, realize the challenges, and look forward to what was available to us as far as tools were concerned to identify the offender," MacDougall said.
Police hoped forensic evidence would be enough

When police announced Irving’s arrest in early 2024, they said the break in the case came thanks to advances in investigative genetic genealogy that linked Irving to one of the DNA samples found at the crime scene.
At a pre-trial hearing, police said Irving's DNA was found on Carr’s body, on a pair of underwear left at the scene and on an extinguished cigarette butt placed in Carr’s navel.
His DNA was not found on the towel used to strangle Carr, nor or on a sock left at the crime scene that police said was likely used as a glove to prevent leaving fingerprints behind.

"I certainly hoped that the forensic evidence would be enough to carry the day,” said former Charlottetown police chief Brad MacConnell, who led the investigation for years and now works as the city's chief administrative officer.
“It became apparent over the last several months as we worked through this that the challenges were too much to overcome."
The man police accused of murdering Byron Carr in 1988 is now free. Here's what happened
But the Crown's office didn’t know about the missing evidence until July — years after Irving’s arrest and just months before the trial was set to begin.
Crown attorney Christopher White said he’s disappointed the case won’t go to trial.
“This was a matter of personal and public significance,” he said.

“I think that everyone involved viewed that it was important that it be adjudicated in a public venue, so for that not to be able to take place, it’s disappointing and I cannot image what it would be like for Mr. Carr’s family.”

Byron Carr was 36 years old when he was murdered in his Charlottetown home in 1988. This poster was displayed at a 2024 news conference when police announced they'd made an arrest in relation to the case. (Wayne Thibodeau/CBC)
Charlottetown police say they haven’t ruled out a third-party review into how evidence is handled, but MacDougall said he’s confident something like this wouldn’t happen now.
The Crown said it won’t reopen the case against Irving.
Despite the outcome, both police and Carr’s family say they’re confident that while there isn’t enough evidence to bring him to trial, the right person was arrested.
“There’s no justice when someone is killed,” said John Carr, Byron’s brother.
“Nothing he could be sentenced to would ever bring Byron back or give us any more satisfaction. We’re not out to get anyone for it, but you know, he’s the one that’s got to live with himself.”
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Devon Goodsell is a senior producer for CBC in Prince Edward Island with a focus on the criminal justice system. She has worked as a CBC journalist in a variety of roles since 2007, including as a producer for CBCNews.ca in Toronto, and as a reporter and associate producer in Vancouver.
With files from Laura Meader, Wayne Thibodeau and Nicola MacLeod

articles.title: Nigel Farage says charities that help asylum seekers get to UK should be prosecuted
articles.summary:
Reform leader did not say who should be targeted but party figures have been critical of small boat rescues by RNLI

Charities and volunteers who help asylum seekers get to the UK should face…

blocks.text: Charities and volunteers who help asylum seekers get to the UK should face potential criminal prosecution, Nigel Farage has said in an interview with a rightwing US podcaster.

While the Reform UK leader did not specify which organisations should be targeted, he and other senior Reform figures have been heavily critical of the Royal National Lifeboat Institution (RNLI), which has faced a campaign of intimidation for its work in rescuing asylum seekers in the Channel.

Speaking to Benny Johnson, a podcaster who has previously written for a series of rightwing US outlets, including Breitbart News, Farage discussed the arrival of asylum seekers on small boats, calling it “literally an invasion of people who could cause us enormous harm”.
Johnson asked him: “Do you believe in criminal penalties for those who facilitated this invasion of the English Isles?”

Farage replied: “Totally, totally. The role of the NGOs, the role of those that are sponsored by taxpayers’ money, because they’re nice, they’re good, they’re kind. They have actually aided and abetted criminality in absolutely every way.

“These are people [who are] are deluded – deluded, hard-left socialist Marxists, who don’t believe in countries, don’t believe in borders, don’t believe in identities, are intent on destroying everything that exists.”

Farage has previously described the RNLI, which rescues some asylum seekers, a small proportion of its lifesaving work, as a “migrant taxi service”, while other Reform figures have criticised the the charity, including sharing footage of far-right protestors abusing RNLI crews bringing people ashore.
Calling for charities and campaign groups to be prosecuted for their work has echoes of the efforts by the former Hungarian prime minister Viktor Orbán to try to cement his grip on power.
A Reform spokesperson said Farage’s comments “speak for themselves”.

In his conversation with Johnson, Farage repeatedly raised what he said was the issue of Muslim asylum seekers arriving in the UK, citing what he said was the example of Michigan, the US state where rightwing agitators have sought to whip up anti-Muslim feeling.
Farage said: “We are importing into our countries … people who will do us enormous harm, who will change, disrupt our lives in every way, in fact make our way of life potentially unrecognisable.”

Saying that European countries such as the UK and France had a greater problem with migration that the US, Farage said if Donald Trump was followed in office by a “weak politician” who did not tackle migration and stand up for “American, English-speaking Christian values” then the consequences would be dire.
He told Johnson: “If we don’t, this show of yours will be illegal in five or 10 years time. Literally, you’ll be banned for hate speech.”
after newsletter promotion

Elsewhere in the interview, Farage speculated that five UK nationals arrested near RAF Fairford late last month before being bailed had been undertaking “a dummy run for a proper terrorist attack on UK forces”.

He added: “I’m deeply, deeply shocked that they’re out on bail whilst there are other people in this country who have said things that the establishment now thinks are racist, who are held inside behind bars without without frankly, proper charge. So It’s what we call here two tier policing.”
Farage has a habit of sometimes making his message more robust for rightwing US audiences.

He has appeared several times on the web TV show hosted by the disgraced far-right pundit Alex Jones, who was sued by bereaved parents of the 2012 Sandy Hook school shooting, which Jones said had been a hoax.
Farage was criticised by some Jewish groups for using these and other US interviews to discuss tropes and conspiracy theories associated with the far right and antisemitism.

articles.title: SC: Senior citizen discounts can't be combined with other discounts
articles.summary: The Supreme Court (SC) has ruled that discounts for senior citizens cannot be combined with other discounts, thus these price reductions cannot be applied on top of other promotions or discounts…

blocks.text: Published October 14, 2026 5:32pm

The Supreme Court (SC) has ruled that discounts for senior citizens cannot be combined with other discounts, thus these price reductions cannot be applied on top of other promotions or discounts provided by businesses.

In a press briefer, the SC said that when goods or services are offered at promotional prices, senior citizens may choose either the promotional discount or the 20% senior citizen discount, whichever gives them greater savings.
"Granting an additional discount beyond what the law allows would unfairly benefit the customer at the business expense," the SC said.

The ruling stemmed from a case filed against a general manager of a hotel in Bacolod City for alleged violation of Republic Act 7432 or the Senior Citizens Act. The hotel executive was acquitted in the ruling.

Under the law, as amended by the Expanded Senior Citizens Act of 2010, Filipinos aged 60 and above are entitled to benefits and privileges, including a 20% discount on services in hotels, restaurants, and recreation centers.
According to the SC, the general manager was charged for refusing to grant two senior citizens their discounts.
However, the general manager argued that the hotel had already applied the 20% discount on the room rate negotiated by a club that the senior citizens were members.
The Municipal Trial Court in Cities, Regional Trial Court, and Court of Appeals found the general manager guilty.
For its part, the SC reversed the rulings, saying the hotel was not required to grant an additional 20% discount.
It said that while the Senior Citizens Act aims to protect and support senior citizens, its implementation must also be fair to businesses.

"[T]he State's pursuit of public welfare cannot be allowed to impose undue or confiscatory burdens on private establishments, whose continued viability is essential to the long-term effectiveness of the law," it said. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Swedish fugitive wanted for fraud nabbed in Negros Oriental
articles.summary: Immigration authorities have arrested a 35-year-old Swedish national in Negros Oriental who is wanted by Finnish authorities for multiple fraud charges and is the subject of an Interpol Red Notice.

blocks.text: October 14, 2026 | 5:29pm
Thirty-five-year-old Swedish national Andre Per Michael Palmqvist arrested by Immigration officials on Oct. 4, 2026.
Bureau of Immigration / Released

MANILA, Philippines — Immigration authorities have arrested a 35-year-old Swedish national in Negros Oriental who is wanted by Finnish authorities for multiple fraud charges and is the subject of an Interpol Red Notice.

In a statement on Wednesday, October 14, the Bureau of Immigration identified the foreign fugitive as Andre Per Michael Palmqvist, who was apprehended on October 4 in Barangay Banilad, Bacong, Negros Oriental, by operatives from the BI Fugitive Search Unit (FSU).
According to the FSU, the operation was carried out following a request from the Nordic Liaison Office in Manila, which alerted Philippine authorities to Palmqvist’s presence in the country.
Finnish authorities issued an arrest warrant against Palmqvist stemming from charges of aggravated fraud and attempted aggravated fraud.
Investigators allege that Palmqvist engaged in deceptive schemes to obtain unlawful financial gain.
In one instance, he purportedly rented property without the intent or capacity to pay rental fees or return the assets, causing the owner an estimated loss of €320,000 (P22,529,280).
In another case, he allegedly attempted to fraudulently acquire heavy tools, mobile phones and fuel, resulting in an additional loss of €11,863 (P835,202.65).
Immigration travel records show that Palmqvist last entered the Philippines on Aug. 21, 2022. He has been overstaying in the country since August 2025.

Palmqvist is currently held at the BI Warden’s Facility at Camp Bagong Diwa in Taguig City, where he remains in custody pending formal deportation proceedings and summary deportation to face trial abroad.

articles.title: 115 families still living in tents in Negros Occidental nearly a year after Tino
articles.summary: The local government is straining its finances to assist displaced families while awaiting national funding for recovery

blocks.text: MOTHER AND DAUGHTER. Dorelyn Dagang cuddles her five-month-old daughter inside their tent on the grounds of Colegio de La Castellana.
Ambo Delilan/Rappler
The local government is straining its finances to assist displaced families while awaiting national funding for recovery

items: Nearly a year after Typhoon Tino, over 100 families in La Castellana, Negros Occidental, are still living in tents with no clear timeline for relocation.
The municipal government has purchased land for a new relocation site, but development and permits are still pending, causing delays in transferring the displaced families.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

NEGROS OCCIDENTAL, Philippines – Nearly a year after Typhoon Tino (Kalmaegi) battered the Visayas, including southern Negros Occidental, over 100 displaced families in La Castellana town are still living in tents, with no clear timeline for their transfer to a permanent relocation site.

For mothers Anna Fernandez, 35, of Lapak-Duldol, and Dorelyn Dagang, 32, of Igpanulong, both in Barangay Robles, the November 4 anniversary of the devastation is a reminder that their ordeal is far from over.
Their families are among 115 displaced households staying in tents provided by the Office of Civil Defense (OCD) on the grounds of Colegio de La Castellana in Barangay Robles.

blocks.caption: MAKESHIFT. Anna Fernandez stands in front of her family’s makeshift shelter for nearly a year after Typhoon Tino. Ambo Delilan/Rappler

blocks.text: In an interview with Rappler on Monday, October 12, Fernandez said living in a tent for nearly a year had taken a toll on her family.
“Kainit, kaging-ot, kag tulo sang ulan ang amon gina-antus sa masami,” she said in Hiligaynon.
(We often endure the heat, stuffiness and leaking rain.)
Even meeting their basic sanitation needs has been difficult, she added.
Fernandez has two children, and her husband relies on daily odd jobs as a cement hauler to support the family.
Dagang, meanwhile, gave birth to her youngest child in a tent last May after losing her home and belongings to Tino while she was three months pregnant.
Now a mother of three with an unemployed husband, she said her greatest wish was for her family to have a permanent home.
“Diyos ko, san-o pa ayhan?” she asked in Hiligaynon. (My God, when will it be?)

The municipal government has purchased a six-hectare property in Barangay Robles for a relocation site, but the transfer of the families, comprising 423 people, cannot proceed until the land is developed and the necessary permits are secured, La Castellana Vice Mayor Alme Rhummyla Nicor-Mangilimutan said.
“We need time. We need money. We need help from the national government,” said Mangilimutan, who also heads the town’s Incident Management Team.
Tino displaced about 1,600 families across La Castellana alone, including 600 from Barangay Robles.
“Wala na gid sila sang puli-an. Kalulu-oy gid sila, actually,” Mangilimutan said.
(They really have no home to return to. They are truly in a pitiful state.)
The municipal government spends about P30,000 daily to feed the families in the tent community, Mangilimutan said.
“It’s financially draining, really,” she said. “But we have no choice; we have to face this as a daily challenge.”

To sustain assistance for the displaced residents, the municipality has been realigning its Maintenance, Operating and Other Expenses (MOOE) budget to cover educational allowances for schoolchildren, as well as burial and medical assistance for affected families.
Despite efforts to secure national government funding, Mangilimutan said the municipality was still waiting for assistance.

La Castellana, one of the localities hardest hit by Tino in the province, has submitted a P300-million recovery proposal, said Donato Sermeno III, director of the Office of Civil Defense in Negros Island Region.

The proposal has been included in the OCD-NIR’s post-disaster needs assessment, which Sermeno said had been submitted to the OCD’s central office in Manila for possible funding through the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund (NDRRMF).

Civil Defense Undersecretary Harold Cabreros pledged to prioritize the endorsement of the OCD-NIR’s assessment for funding through the OCD and the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NDRRMC).
Sermeno has yet to disclose the total amount proposed under the assessment for the entire Negros Island Region.

Other local governments seeking assistance for Tino victims through the PDNA include the cities of Bago, La Carlota and Himamaylan; the towns of Moises Padilla, Isabela, Binalbagan, Hinigaran and Pontevedra in Negros Occidental; and Canlaon City in Negros Oriental. – Rappler.com

articles.title: El Niño may affect small pelagic fish catch, says fishers group
articles.summary: The potentially strong El Niño may affect fishing activities, including the catch of small pelagic fishes, a fishers group said on Wednesday.

blocks.text: Published October 14, 2026 5:24pm
The potentially strong El Niño may affect fishing activities, including the catch of small pelagic fishes, a fishers group said on Wednesday.

“Basically, it is possible that the fishing catch will change. But for now, it is still in normal conditions,” said Association of Fresh Fish Traders of the Philippines president Jonjon Santos in an interview with Super Radyo dzBB in Filipino.
“The most affected will be the small pelagics, such as the galunggong (round scad), sardines. They are very sensitive to temperatures, the so-called water column,” he added.
El Niño occurs when sea surface temperature rises, according to PAGASA.
The state weather bureau earlier said that average temperature across the Philippines is set to rise by 1 to 2 degrees Celsius during the weather phenomenon.
Citing the 1983 strong El Niño, the group said that fish production dropped significantly after a year.
“So it means that for small fish, the water column or thermocline can be strong,” said Santos.
The group said that it has yet to monitor any cases of unwarranted price increase in fish products as it is closed fishing season.
“When November comes, until February, you know, we are in closed fishing season. So there is no production,” said Santos. —RF, GMA News

articles.title: Dropping 3 impeachment articles vs Sara, who benefits?
articles.summary: The faster we get to a vote, the sooner everyone who wants to imagine a 2028 playing field without Sara Duterte can start planning for it

blocks.text: The faster we get to a vote, the sooner everyone who wants to imagine a 2028 playing field without Sara Duterte can start planning for it

It’s a move that confused impeachment trial spectators and prompted lead defense lawyer Sheila Sison to fire off a sharp litany of tirades — so why, really, did the prosecution abandon three of the four impeachment articles against Vice President Sara Duterte?
There are official reasons, and then ones that emerge when you look at who stands to benefit.

The official reason, as lead prosecutor Jinky Luistro manifested before the court, in dropping most cases against the Vice President is to speed up the trial amid growing “public impatience,” and respect for the Senate’s other legislative responsibilities — from passing pending bills to working on the 2027 national budget.
In a subsequent press conference, the prosecution tried to sell the move as beneficial to the Vice President.

“If I were the Vice President, I would even thank the prosecution because now, she can focus on one (case),” private prosecutor Lorna Kapunan said, referring to the retained charge on unexplained wealth.

blocks.caption: Dropping 3 impeachment articles vs Sara, who benefits?

blocks.text: While Senate President Chiz Escudero sided with the prosecution in allowing the withdrawal of three impeachment articles, it is difficult to dismiss Sison’s argument: that her client was being denied the opportunity to present counter-evidence in open court on two of the three dropped articles, after the prosecution had already presented its evidence on them.
“The prosecution cannot be allowed to have the benefit of its accusations without bearing the burden of having those accusations tested,” Sison said, warning of a potential mistrial.
So, if not the Vice President, whom does this move really serve?
Of course, the prosecution won’t drop this bombshell, perhaps calculated, move without knowing for certain that there are more pros than cons to this.
Behind closed doors, the prosecution is crunching the numbers too, and there’s growing confidence that they have enough to secure a guilty verdict.

If all senators from the majority vote to remove the Vice President from office, the reduced conviction threshold of 14 votes is met. There is a desire to hit 16 votes to prevent any Supreme Court action by the defense, but that means courting the harder-to-sway senators — Camille Villar, Pia Cayetano, or even the absent Loren Legarda.

With the prosecution abandoning the three impeachment articles, two of which they already exhaustively presented before the court, the defense team gets no chance to provide counter-evidence for the senator-judges to evaluate.

This means that the defense doesn’t have the power to prolong the trial the same way they availed of every objection during the prosecution’s turn, because the cases that the prosecution dropped will no longer be adjudicated by the court.
From the prosecution’s perspective, the faster they get to the vote, the better, especially if they believe they have convinced enough senator-judges to side with them.

Senators have undergone their most grueling work schedule in years due to the trial — attending court proceedings in the morning, and fulfilling their legislative responsibilities in the afternoon and rest of the day.
Even Majority Leader Migz Zubiri quipped that he was tired from the 12-hour duty.
So why prolong the proceedings if they already know how they will vote in the trial?

Had the three cases not been dropped, senators would have set themselves up for an exhausting final two months of 2026. November is known to be a busy month due to budget deliberations in the Senate. The ASEAN Summit in Manila is also expected to disrupt their schedule.
A conviction not only removes the Vice President from office, but also quashes her 2028 presidential aspirations.
Barring Duterte from the race levels the playing field and removes the clear front-runner.
This is advantageous for senator-judges, many of whom have gunned for, or are gunning for, higher office.

Senator Risa Hontiveros is exploring a 2028 presidential bid. Others have tried but failed to be president or vice president in the past — Ping Lacson, Tito Sotto, Kiko Pangilinan, Escudero who interestingly quickly came up with the ruling that sided with the prosecution’s surprise motion, and even Duterte-allied senators Alan Cayetano and Loren Legarda.
The Tulfo brothers and senators Bam Aquino, Robin Padilla, and Bong Go have also been floated as presidential or vice presidential contenders in the 2028 polls.
Putting the impeachment saga behind in 2026 gives other hopefuls time to reposition, build alliances, and decide where they want to place their bets for 2028. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Fact check: Misleading graph about alleged Russian bot activity
articles.summary: Did attacks on Russian data centers reduce bot activity around Germany's AfD? A viral graph claims they did. But it contains significant inconsistencies and provides no evidence to support the claim.

image.caption: The graph shows significant inconsistencies, and its data source is unclearImage: x.com/tomaszdechovsky

blocks.text: After Ukrainian drone attacks on data centers operated by the Russian technology company Yandex, claims began circulating online that the strikes had disrupted or even halted the activity of Russian propaganda bots. These accounts are often accused of spreading disinformation or artificially amplifying content on social media.

During the Warsaw Security Forum, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy also suggested that the attacks on Yandex data centers had disrupted bot activity, saying "there was less hate, less division, and fewer provocations [because] there were fewer bots." In response to BBC Verify, Zelenskyy's office said that, rather than referring to reduced bot activity, the president was "talking about the atmosphere on social media." The office added that it had seen "reports of fewer provocative and hateful comments" from many social media users.

So far, however, there is no clear evidence linking the attacks to a decline in bot activity. According to Josef Holnburger, managing director of the Center for Monitoring, Analysis and Strategy (CeMAS), there is currently "no decline in Russian disinformation activities that could be explained by the attack on Yandex data centers." CeMAS systematically monitors such campaigns.
European lawmaker shares graph without evidence on X

Nevertheless, a misleading graph has been circulated as supposed evidence. It was shared, for example, by Czech Member of the European Parliament Tomáš Zdechovský. His post was viewed more than four million times on X. He suggested that the graph might demonstrate a decline in "online activity around AfD," although he did not specify what kind of activity he meant. In reality, the graph most likely demonstrates nothing at all.

blocks.caption: A Czech Member of the European Parliament linked the graph to an alleged decline in online activity surrounding the AfDImage: x.com/tomaszdechovsky

blocks.text: The German-language graph is titled "Daily activity over 3 months." It appears to show activity remaining relatively stable before dropping sharply in early October, roughly coinciding with the attacks on Yandex data centers. However, nothing in the graph itself indicates that this relates to AfD-related online activity.
No source and faulty scaling

The same applies to the graph's underlying data. It is unclear which data were used. No source is provided, nor is there any explanation of the data collection process or calculation method for the alleged "activity," which initially ranges between 6,000 and 7,000 before falling below 3,000.

Particularly striking is that the graph extends to October 15. Its final data point appears to correspond to October 14 – a date that was still in the future when the graph first appeared online on October 11. Data for a future date cannot exist.

The graph also contains scaling errors on both the X and Y axes. For example, on the Y axis, the distance between 2,500 and 3,000 is smaller than the other 500-unit intervals. Because the Y axis does not begin at zero, the decline is visually exaggerated. On the X axis, equal periods of time are represented by unequal distances.

It is also unclear which platforms were analyzed and how the variable "activity" was calculated. The absence of a known data source, the inaccurate scaling, and the inclusion of "future" values strongly suggest that this is not a meaningful graph based on factual data and sound statistical methods.
AI involvement cannot be proven, but is possible
It is unclear whether AI was used to create the graph. Given the errors and the apparent "hallucination" of presenting future data, AI involvement cannot be ruled out.

Misleading and error-filled graphs, some of which may have been AI-generated, appear regularly. German public broadcaster BR's #Faktenfuchs team recently reported on one such graph that falsely depicted industrial production in Germany (article in German). False or fabricated graphs can lend credibility to unsupported claims.
The identity of the graph's creator remains unknown.
What do Cloudflare data actually show?

Cloudflare data are also frequently cited in connection with claims of declining bot activity. However, according to CeMAS managing director Holnburger, there is a misunderstanding about what Cloudflare's report actually means. Cloudflare provides services to many websites that block traffic assessed as non-human. Automated web traffic is common and includes, for example, crawlers that check websites for freshly published content. Search engines, including Yandex, rely on these crawlers. Other bots may be used for spam in comment sections.
In a message to #Faktenfuchs Holnburger writes, "a decline in bot activity on websites is something entirely different from a decline in inauthentic behavior by social bots on social networks."

Referring to Cloudflare data, he added: "When looking at overall activity from Russian IP addresses on servers using Cloudflare services, there is no major decline in bot activity." Furthermore, there is no reason to assume that the infrastructure used by disinformation-related social bots would be hosted on Yandex data centers. "It is more likely that these systems are distributed across many different providers," Holnburger writes.
The article was originally written in German and adapted into English by Alima de Graaf

articles.title: Bank of England and IMF bosses issue stark warning on cyber threat to trust
articles.summary: Andrew Bailey and Kristalina Georgieva voice concerns about financial system on panel about online fraud

blocks.text: The heads of the Bank of England and the International Monetary Fund have issued a stark warning that rising cyber-attacks risk undermining trust in the financial system.

Speaking on a panel about online fraud at the IMF and World Bank meetings in Bangkok, the governor of the Bank of England, Andrew Bailey, pointed to alarming headlines about self-replicating AI agents hijacking personal devices, and the French supermarket hack that heated fridges up to 50C.
“If you try to say what’s at the heart of this debate about AI – for me, it’s about trust in technology and it’s about human control to achieve that trust in technology,” he said.
Pointing to the key importance of technology in underpinning today’s financial system, he added: “If we don’t have trust in money, we don’t operate as a society.”
Echoing his concerns, the IMF’s managing director, Kristalina Georgieva, said the toll of cyber fraud was now so great that people could decide to opt out of the formal financial system altogether.
“I was born and grew up on the other side of the iron curtain,” the Bulgarian economist said. “We didn’t trust the system. What did we do? I would have my dollars in a shoebox under my bed.

“And I worry, today, that unless we figure out how to get ahead of this curve, given the speed, the scale and the cost of fraud growing up, we may end up with lots of people with shoeboxes under their beds.”

She said this threat was particularly acute for people on the fringes of the financial system. “Imagine what would happen if trust disappears or is eroded to a point that people no more have the courage to be included,” she said.

Her comments followed a warning from the IMF on Tuesday that the possibility of a big cyber-attack was one of the factors raising the global financial stability threat level to “elevated”, alongside higher borrowing costs and the risk of an AI share price crash.
Bailey stressed that fraud was now frequently committed via social media platforms and apps, not just traditional financial channels – and urged big tech to take responsibility.
He contrasted today’s environment with the legal status in the UK of outlets such as newspapers, which are responsible for the veracity of everything they publish.
after newsletter promotion

Instead, the governor said: “We’ve moved into quite an extreme position of, well, these platforms are open to everybody and there’s no real liability to the provision of the platform to what’s on it. Guess what? Everything’s on it. You know, the good, the bad and the incredibly ugly and downright criminal and terrible.”

He added: “I don’t go around pointing the finger at people and saying: ‘You’re bad.’ What I have said is: ‘Look, there is responsibility all around.’ And we need to evolve to a world where everybody understands this responsibility, and everybody is then a part of addressing the problem.”
He added: “We must get the social media companies involved because a lot of this fraud is transmitted through those channels.”

Bailey called for the same tools that are being used by cybercriminals to be put to work protecting the financial system. “I’m going to use a sporting metaphor: this technology is arming the offence but it can also arm the defence, and it must do.”
The panel event at which the pair were speaking was to launch a new set of international principles for avoiding cyber fraud in financial institutions, called the Bangkok blueprint.

articles.title: Minnesota professor linked to series of bizarre incidents involving urine at university
articles.summary:
Investigators determined professor responsible for urine found on a backpack, in trash cans and in water bottles

A former professor at Macalester College in the
articles.byline: Keely Aouga and Ramon Antonio Vargas

blocks.text: A former professor at Macalester College in the Minnesota city of St Paul is facing a felony charge for allegedly spilling his urine on a student’s backpack while he still worked at the school, costing more than $2,000 in damages, according to a state criminal court document.

Paul Fischer, 55, is at the center of the bizarre, alleged workplace misconduct case that led to his being cited for first-degree damage to property – and linked to at least a half dozen such incidents involving urine at the liberal arts college over the course of a year.

St Paul police homed in on Fischer after a student reported that she left her belongings unattended for about six minutes on 5 December in a common area near his office. Fischer was a biology professor at the time. The student told police that she found urine on her backpack when she returned to her belongings, according to the criminal court document obtained by the Guardian.

The student reported the matter in February to St Paul police. Police learned that the college by then had also investigated her complaint – and determined there had been at least six such episodes involving urine at the school’s Olin-Rice science center during the span of about a year.
Urination had been found in trash cans, individuals’ water bottles and inside professors’ decorations, the state criminal court document said.
Investigators determined Fischer was responsible for the series of urine-related cases, and he resigned from Macalester College, where he had spent 25 years working.

Authorities confronted Fischer before charging him, the court document said. He allegedly shared that “during the last one and a half to two years he developed a habit of urinating in a cup and disposing the contents in either trash cans or lab sinks around campus”, according to the document.

The former professor allegedly claimed that he was emptying a container of urine into a trash can near his office on the day that the student who reported him said her backpack had been damaged. He said he believed that the cup of urine spilled on to the student’s belongings, the court document alleged.
The urine on the student’s backpack resulted in damage to both the bag and her belongings inside, the document added.
The student provided investigators with an itemized receipt for what was damaged that amounted to $2,070.

Prosecutors for Ramsey county, Minnesota, whose jurisdiction includes St Paul, charged Fischer through a criminal complaint on 7 October. He could get up to five years in prison as well as a maximum fine of $10,000 if convicted as charged.
A spokesperson for Macalester College on Tuesday said the school “is aware of the criminal charge against Paul Fischer” – and that his employment there ended during the 2025-2026 academic year.
“As this is an ongoing legal matter involving a former employee, the college has no further comment,” the spokesperson said.
Attempts to contact Fischer on Tuesday were not immediately successful.
Commentary about the criminal complaint against Fischer made its way over to a page under his name on the RateMyProfessors.com platform.
“So that explains the yellowish stain that appeared on my lab coat,” a comment posted on Tuesday read.
The comment, which the Guardian could not authenticate, also said: “I don’t understand what motivates someone to do something like this, but avoid him at all costs.”

articles.title: As this couple cycles through their grief, a vaccine to save other babies is tested
articles.summary: Months after the death of their baby girl, Carly Wedge and Alexandre Genest are touring around Nova Scotia on their bicycles — working through their grief, raising money for the hospital that tried…

image.caption: Alexandre Genest and Carly Wedge are cycling around Nova Scotia to raise money for the IWK Health Centre, and awareness about Group B Streptococcus disease, which killed their infant daughter in April 2026. (Paul Poirier/CBC)

blocks.text: Nova Scotia·New

Months after the death of their baby girl, Carly Wedge and Alexandre Genest are touring around Nova Scotia on their bicycles — working through their grief, raising money for the hospital that tried to save her, and spreading the word about a vaccine that’s in development.
A vaccine against the illness that killed 3-week-old Lupine Genest is in clinical trials
The pregnancy, the birth and the early days of parenthood were the fulfilment of their dreams.
“She was pretty lively,” said Alexandre Genest, remembering his daughter, Lupine, as an infant. “She had long hair already.”
“And big, sparkly eyes,” added his wife, Carly Wedge, Lupine’s mom.

But after just three weeks with their "perfectly healthy" baby, the new parents were plunged into their worst nightmare. At their home on Nova Scotia’s South Shore, Lupine suddenly turned ill, and her parents took her to the nearby regional hospital. Doctors ordered that she be sent to Halifax’s children’s hospital, where she was taken into intensive care.
Five days later, she was gone.
A picture of Lupine Genest follows her dad's bicycle as he travels around Nova Scotia's highways and trails. (Paul Poirier/CBC)

Lupine was infected by Group B Streptococcus, or GBS, which led to sepsis and meningitis. GBS is a common bacterium that many adults carry without symptoms, but it causes life-threatening illness in babies.

Pregnant women are often screened for GBS, and if they test positive, they’re given a preventative round of antibiotics during labour. The antibiotics can protect newborns during the first week of life, but not beyond. For cases that begin later in infancy, such as Lupine’s, there is no means of prevention — yet.

Now, as Lupine would be turning six months old, Wedge and Genest are touring around Nova Scotia on their bicycles — working through their grief, raising money for the hospital that tried to save her, and spreading the word about a vaccine that’s in development.
“It's a rare thing, what happened to Lupine, but I think when it happens to you, it doesn't really matter that it's rare and you just want something to change,” said Wedge.
“A cure,” added Genest.
A vaccine on the horizon

What makes GBS so dangerous is that it escalates very quickly, said Dr. Joanne Langley, pediatric infectious disease specialist at the IWK Health Centre — the children's hospital where Lupine was treated.
“By the time you get the baby to care and start care, the baby has often become very unwell. And so even our best treatment will not catch up, in some cases.
"Preventing this disease is the best strategy,” she said.
Dr. Joanne Langley is an infectious disease specialist at the IWK Health Centre and investigator at the Canadian Center for Vaccinology. (Galen McRae/CBC)
Langley is an investigator at the Canadian Center for Vaccinology, and she’s working on a Phase 3 clinical trial for a maternal GBS vaccine.

Researchers have been trying to develop a vaccine against GBS since the 1970s, but Langley said no attempt has advanced as far as the current one, by Pfizer. Depending on how the current trial progresses, and on regulatory approvals, she said the vaccine could be widely available in the next few years.
“This will be just an overwhelming advance in the care of women and babies,” said Langley.

The World Health Organization says GBS causes about 150,000 stillbirths and infant deaths globally, each year, and vaccines could prevent more than 50 per cent of infant GBS cases. GBS can also lead to preterm birth, and a vaccine may lower that risk, too, according to the WHO.
Wedge and Genest say their baby girl, Lupine, was perfectly healthy for the first three weeks of her life. Then she suddenly turned severely ill. (Martha Wedge/Submitted)
In addition to preventing illness and death, Langley said the vaccine could also reduce the use of antibiotics in pregnant women who screen positive.
“That's a good thing, because the normal bacteria that mom has on her skin and her vagina are all healthy and part of the newborn's eventual microbiome,” she said.
Pfizer is testing the vaccine at more than 200 locations across the globe, including four in Canada.
Wedge said it feels like serendipity that the clinical trial started in Nova Scotia shortly after Lupine’s death.
"The more I learn about GBS, the more passionate I feel about making sure something is done to hopefully prevent other families from going through what we went through," she said.
Alexandre Genest and Carly Wedge stand by their bicycles at Summerville Beach Provincial Park, N.S., in early October 2026. (Jake Foley/Submitted)
As she and Genest cycle along Nova Scotia's rural roads and trails, they’re pulling a small trailer displaying Lupine’s picture, and sharing their journey on social media.

They said it’s been healing, talking to people about their daughter. At the same time, they’re trying to get people interested in the vaccine; they want to see the clinical trial get all the participants it needs.
“We're trying to get the word out to as many people who might be interested as possible, to help them push the science forward,” said Wedge.
Langley said because of the newness of the vaccine, the risks are unknown. The current study is specifically meant to test its safety.
Langley said investigators have not seen any serious events associated with the shot, so far. She said another trial may be needed to test the vaccine's efficacy in preventing disease.

articles.title: Cardinal David: Send Pope Leo XIV a 'hug' following lung cancer diagnosis
articles.summary: Cardinal Pablo Virgilio David on Wednesday called on the Filipino faithful to send Pope Leo XIV a "hug" through prayer after the leader of the Roman Catholic Church was diagnosed with cancer…

blocks.text: Published October 14, 2026 4:56pm

Cardinal Pablo Virgilio David on Wednesday called on the Filipino faithful to send Pope Leo XIV a "hug" through prayer after the leader of the Roman Catholic Church was diagnosed with cancer following his lung surgery.
In a social media post, David shared that he briefly encountered the Pope during the celebration of the Feast of Our Lady of the Rosary at the Vatican.
"Last Wednesday, he (Pope Leo XIV) reached out to me with a hug. Today, I want to return that hug through prayer. And I invite you to do the same," David said.
"Let us surround our Holy Father with the warmth of our prayers, that he may feel himself embraced by the whole Church, just as he has embraced so many of us with the love of a brother," he added.

According to the Vatican medical bulletin, Pope Leo XIV has lung adenocarcinoma, a common form of cancer, with tissue tests conducted during the operation confirming what doctors had suspected from preparatory examinations.
He was admitted to Rome's Gemelli hospital on Tuesday for surgery to remove the growth that doctors had discovered in a recent routine health check.
The surgery was successful with no complications after it lasted about 90 minutes.

blocks.caption: Courtesy: Pablo Virgilio David/ Facebook

blocks.text: Courtesy: Pablo Virgilio David/ Facebook
David described his encounter and hug from the Pope as a "simple embrace" where a "brother quietly asking to be accompanied in prayer."

"It was only last Sunday, when he announced that he would undergo lung surgery and asked the faithful for their spiritual closeness and prayers, that I found myself remembering that embrace. And I thought, 'So that's why his hug felt that way,'" David said.
As Pope Leo XIV's recover following his surgery, Cardinal Luis Antonio Tagle presides the Eucharistic celebration at the Vatican on Wednesday. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Saudi Aramco administrative building attacked, limited fire reported
articles.summary: An administrative building belonging to Saudi Arabia's state-owned oil company Saudi Aramco in the eastern city of Dhahran was attacked, causing a limited fire, the Energy Ministry said in a…

image.caption: Storage tanks are seen at the North Jeddah bulk plant, an Aramco oil facility, in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, on March 21, 2021. Saudi Arabia said Friday, May 31, 2024, it will sell a second sliver of stock in its state oil giant Aramco worth billions of dollars, its first tranche since its initial public

blocks.text: World·New

An administrative building belonging to Saudi Arabia's state-owned oil company Saudi Aramco in the eastern city of Dhahran was attacked, causing a limited fire, the Energy Ministry said in a statement on Wednesday as fighting between Yemen's Iran-allied Houthis and the kingdom intensified.
Authorities say drones and missiles also intercepted and destroyed in Riyadh
Authorities responded to the incident late on Tuesday and took necessary measures, the ministry said, adding that there were no injuries or deaths.

A company source told Reuters earlier that a ballistic missile hit the Aramco headquarters complex in Dhahran. The source said an office tower in the complex was struck and that its top three floors were damaged. The source and two other people with knowledge of the matter said the building was on fire.
The complex hosts a major operations centre for Aramco, which oversees a vast network of onshore and offshore oil rigs, pipelines, refineries and export terminals.

items: Saudis say Riyadh airport struck for 2nd day in a row, separate airport also attacked

blocks.text: The Houthis have for a week been firing ballistic missiles and drones at key Saudi sites in retaliation for the kingdom's backing of government forces in Yemen's reignited civil war. Riyadh’s international airport has received four strikes, including one on Saturday that killed 13 people.
Follows deadly airport strike
Saturday's ballistic missile strike on Riyadh airport was the deadliest in Saudi Arabia in a decade, with further attacks grounding flights across the country.
Earlier, six sources told Reuters they heard loud booms near the Aramco complex.
The Saudi-led coalition said fragments of a missile that it had intercepted and destroyed in Dhahran had fallen on a residential area, without providing further details.

Surveillance footage shows smoke and fire as people react at the moment of an attack at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, October 10, 2026, in this frame from a handout video. (Saudi Ministry of Media/Reuters)
Authorities also reported that drones and missiles were intercepted and destroyed in the capital, Riyadh, and the country's southern region.

Four people were injured in Riyadh after fragments from two Houthi missiles fell following their interception and destruction, Saudi Civil Defense said on Wednesday. The debris caused limited damage to 15 homes in the capital, the Civil Defense spokesperson said, adding that the injured were two women, a man and a child.

The Houthis had threatened a "harsh and painful" response to Saudi-led strikes on the Yemeni capital Sanaa, with spokesperson Yahya Saree saying targets could include the Saudi Aramco headquarters in Dhahran and an oil refinery in Riyadh.
Oil workers warned
The group has warned oil workers in Saudi Arabia to stay away from sites that could be targets.
The Houthis earlier on Tuesday said Saudi Arabia was attacking Sanaa, and the Saudi-led coalition warned civilians to stay away from an oil depot on the city's outskirts.
Houthi-run Al-Masirah television reported that the Saudi-led coalition had targeted the Yemen Petroleum Company's Sabah central station, a fuel depot on the outskirts of Sanaa.

items: Saudi-led coalition vows retaliation after deadly Houthi attack on Riyadh airport

blocks.text: The coalition said in a statement on Tuesday evening that it attacked the station and other sites in an operation aimed at "neutralizing the capabilities of Houthis" to threaten Saudi Arabia, Yemen and international waterways.
Saudis resume military campaign in Yemen

The Saudi cabinet, chaired by de facto ruler Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, issued a statement on Tuesday before the strike on Saudi Aramco saying the Houthis would face consequences for their repeated attacks on the kingdom.

Saudi Arabia resumed its military campaign in Yemen in support of the internationally recognized government in a bid to reverse the Houthis' sudden gains last month, when they swept down the Red Sea coast to the critical Bab el-Mandeb Strait.

The strait, the southern gateway to the Red Sea, has become a more vital route for Saudi and other global energy supplies since the start of the Iran war in February, when Tehran closed the Strait of Hormuz leading from the Gulf to the Indian Ocean.
While a government offensive that began a week ago pushed the Houthis from the area closest to the strait, the group remains embedded nearby and has made gains around the city of Taiz this month.
How Yemen’s Houthis could supercharge global trade disruptions
Saudi Arabia has been seeking wider support from allies for its campaign against the Houthis and to help it ward off their missile and drone attacks.
Washington, Saudi Arabia's strongest ally and longtime security guarantor, has so far rebuffed Saudi efforts to bring it directly into the war against the Houthis.
The Yemen conflict has resumed as a spillover from the wider US-Iran war that began with the US-Israeli attack on the Islamic Republic on February 28.

Iran, Saudi Arabia's longtime regional rival, has offered to mediate between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis, its foreign minister Abbas Araqchi said on Sunday in statements reiterated by the ministry on Monday.
